Oral α-galactosidase, a digestive enzyme, may help alleviate irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) symptoms in some individuals. However, the current evidence does not support its routine use as a treatment for IBS.

A few studies have investigated the potential benefits of oral α-galactosidase in reducing gastrointestinal symptoms, but these findings are inconsistent and limited by methodological flaws. While some patients reported improvement in their symptoms after taking α-galactosidase supplements, the clinical response was often short-lived or not consistently effective.

Moreover, there is no conclusive evidence to suggest that oral α-galactosidase reliably relieves IBS symptoms. The gastrointestinal (GI) side effects associated with its administration may also be coincidental in some cases, and irritation of the GI tract cannot be entirely ruled out.

In summary, while oral α-galactosidase may offer some benefits for certain individuals with IBS, the current evidence is not strong enough to support its routine use as a treatment. More research is needed to better understand the potential benefits and risks of this enzyme in the context of IBS.
